items.q: Match the following thyroiditis to its feature — 1) Hashimoto 2) Subacute (de Quervain) 3) Postpartum 4) Acute suppurative … A) Painless firm goitre with anti-TPO B) Painful tender thyroid with raised ESR C) Within 12 months of delivery D) Bacterial, painful, requires drainage
items.exp: Hashimoto presents with painless firm goitre and high anti-TPO; subacute thyroiditis is painful with raised ESR; postpartum thyroiditis occurs within 12 months of delivery; acute suppurative thyroiditis is bacterial and needs drainage. (Book p914)

items.q: A 28-year-old woman 5 months postpartum has painless thyroid enlargement with suppressed TSH and raised anti-TPO. The most likely diagnosis is:
items.exp: Painless thyroid dysfunction within 12 months of delivery with positive anti-TPO fits postpartum thyroiditis. (Book p914)

items.q: Assess postpartum thyroiditis: I It typically follows a thyrotoxic then hypothyroid course. II It is usually self-limiting.
items.exp: Postpartum thyroiditis often biphasic (toxic → hypo) and resolves within 12–18 months; some patients progress to permanent hypothyroidism. (Book p914)

items.q: Which is the odd one out — a feature distinguishing subacute thyroiditis from Graves?
items.exp: Painless diffuse goitre with bruit is Graves; tenderness, very high ESR and low uptake are subacute thyroiditis. (Book p914)

items.q: The classic viral prodrome and painful thyroid of subacute thyroiditis is treated symptomatically with ___.
items.exp: Subacute thyroiditis is treated with NSAIDs for pain and beta-blocker for thyrotoxic symptoms; thionamides are not effective. (Book p914)

items.q: Match the following thyroiditis to its uptake scan — 1) Hashimoto 2) Subacute 3) Postpartum 4) Acute suppurative … A) Variable B) Low uptake C) Low uptake D) Low uptake (cold abscess)
items.exp: Hashimoto uptake is variable; subacute, postpartum and acute suppurative thyroiditis all show low uptake due to glandular destruction. (Book p914)

items.q: A 35-year-old has neck pain, fever 38.5 °C and a tender thyroid with ESR 90 mm/h one week after a viral URI. The most consistent diagnosis is:
items.exp: Painful tender thyroid with high ESR after a viral illness fits subacute (de Quervain) thyroiditis. (Book p914)

items.q: Assess thyroiditis treatment: I Antithyroid drugs are first-line for subacute thyroiditis. II NSAIDs are effective for the pain of subacute thyroiditis.
items.exp: NSAIDs (and corticosteroids in severe cases) manage pain; thionamides are not effective because hormone is released, not synthesised. (Book p914)

items.q: Match the following thyroiditis to the preferred treatment — 1) Subacute 2) Postpartum 3) Acute suppurative 4) Hashimoto with hypothyroidism … A) NSAIDs + beta-blocker B) Beta-blocker ± levothyroxine C) IV antibiotics + drainage D) Levothyroxine replacement
items.exp: Subacute thyroiditis uses NSAIDs and beta-blocker; postpartum thyroiditis is supportive with beta-blocker and levothyroxine in the hypothyroid phase; acute suppurative thyroiditis needs IV antibiotics and drainage; hypothyroid Hashimoto needs levothyroxine. (Book p914)

items.q: A patient has fever, severe neck pain and fluctuant thyroid swelling with overlying erythema. The most appropriate next step is:
items.exp: Acute suppurative thyroiditis is a surgical infection requiring IV antibiotics and drainage. (Book p914)

items.q: Postpartum thyroiditis occurs within ___ months of delivery.
items.exp: Postpartum thyroiditis is defined within 12 months of delivery, often biphasic with recovery over 12–18 months. (Book p914)

items.q: Assess thyroiditis associations: I Subacute thyroiditis may follow mumps, measles or coxsackievirus. II Painless thyroiditis is typically postpartum.
items.exp: Subacute thyroiditis is associated with viral infections; painless thyroiditis typically refers to postpartum and silent variants. (Book p914)
